proof_summary: For fixed C>=0, v2(phi(n))>=floor(log2 n)-C forces oddpart(phi(n))<B=2^(C+1). Distinct odd prime factors have p=1+d*2^r with odd d<B; large p>B appear only once. A weighted partition bound gives #E_C(X)<=(R+1)D_B exp(2 sqrt(BR))=X^o(1). Termwise integrality of a near-log window implies a nearmax endpoint. More substantially the exact sliding-window numerator recurrence A_(N+1,L)=2A_(N,L)-2^L phi(N+1)+phi(N+L+1) implies that *adjacent integral full finite sums* force 2^L|phi(N+L+1), hence at most X^o(1) such pairs and at most X/2+X^o(1)+O(1) starts with an integral whole finite sum. This does not bound distance of a nonintegral finite sum to Z or the infinite tail error.
